paragraphs: The following assessments concern basic nursing and patient-safety working methods, without predicting hiring, licensing or professional titles.

U.S. LPN/LVNs provide basic nursing care within their state scope and training: observing and recording patient information, assisting with daily care, performing permitted ordered tasks, and communicating with the care team. The list is not a universal clinical sequence or authorization to perform every task.

This fictional record-checking exercise involves no patients, medicines or equipment. Source record: patient N01, 09:00, temperature 36.8°C, pulse 78/min, blood pressure 118/76 mmHg. A separate unresolved record is labelled N02, 09:10, with medication status “order unverified; administration not documented.” The handover has no recipient. A draft changes N01’s pulse to 87/min and states “medication administered at 09:10.” List the source information, discrepancies, unknowns and questions for authorized review. Do not interpret clinical status, select medicines or doses, or write a dressing procedure. Work at your own pace; completion speed does not establish clinical competence. Review reference: identify 78→87, the unresolved N01/N02 mismatch, unsupported administration status and the missing handover recipient. Preserve source values and flag unknowns without inventing a clinical conclusion. A paper exercise can explore interest in careful record checking; it cannot establish tolerance for standing, patient handling or shift work. Explore those demands separately through the specific job and appropriate arrangements.

People interested in helping others, careful source checking and team communication may wish to explore the work further. Interest or a paper exercise does not establish clinical competence, licensure or tolerance for shifts and physical demands; check those separately against the specific role and appropriate training.

U.S. licensed practical nurses (LPNs) and licensed vocational nurses (LVNs) provide basic nursing care, generally under registered-nurse or physician supervision. Medication, IV duties and direct-supervision requirements depend on the state, training and institutional authorization. These U.S. licenses are not equivalent to mainland Chinese nurse registration or advanced-practice qualifications.

entries: Work objects: patient vital signs/symptoms, orders/medication lists, nursing/medication records, wounds/catheters and other care sites, samples/supplies and patient-safety/privacy requirements.
Inspectable outputs: vital-sign/observation records, medication/check records, wound/catheter-care records, sample collection/submission records, patient/family communication and abnormality reports.

Task illustration, not a fixed clinical sequence: review authorized care information, observe and record, carry out permitted care, and communicate or hand over to the team. Urgent response and reporting must not wait for routine care or documentation to finish.

paragraphs: Key judgments: Verify orders under institutional medication/patient-identification procedures, recognize/report abnormalities promptly and confirm procedures fall within state licensing/institutional authorization. Examples are not complete clinical protocols or proof that all LPNs have identical medication authority.

Environment and pace: Often in nursing/residential care facilities, hospitals, clinics and homes, requiring prolonged standing, walking and patient moving, often shifts/night work. Pace depends on patient numbers and changing conditions.

Examples include electronic care records, vital-sign measurement equipment and supplies appropriate to permitted care and personal protection. Specific devices and their use depend on the job, training and authorization; this is not a universal equipment list.

Collaboration chain: patients/families, RNs/nursing supervisors, doctors/other clinicians, pharmacies/laboratories, nursing aides/support staff. Report beyond-authority matters or sudden deterioration under orders/escalation procedures.
Quality standards: accurate/reviewable medication/care records, timely vital signs/observations, infection-control/privacy compliance and complete abnormality reporting/handovers.

LPN/LVN, RN, nursing assistant and advanced practice nurse are distinct qualifications/duties. RN/higher roles need separate education, examinations and registration. Verify state clinical scopes; summaries cannot imply uniform nationwide permissions.

Registered nurses assess care needs, develop and implement nursing care plans, and maintain records. LPN/LVNs provide basic care within their licensed scope. Moving into an RN role requires meeting the destination state’s separate education, examination and registration requirements.

Nursing assistants mainly support daily living and basic care. State-approved training, competency examinations, licensing or certification, and registry requirements vary; these roles should not be described as generally unlicensed. LPN/LVNs require their own state license and work within applicable state and institutional limits.

Advanced practice nurses take on advanced clinical responsibilities, but independent-practice and prescribing authority depend on the state and role. An LPN/LVN license does not itself confer those permissions.

Postsecondary nursing teachers focus on courses, clinical instruction and student assessment. LPN/LVNs focus on authorized patient care and may also provide patient education or approved staff guidance.
AI impact boundaries for licensed practical and vocational nurses

This page has not established verifiable occupation-specific evidence for task-level AI effects, so no quantitative impact score is provided. Record drafts and reminder organization are proposed scenarios for evaluation, not evidence of clinical effectiveness, adoption or job loss.
Occupational sources describe LPN/LVN actual tasks/objects. Record tool capability, organizational adoption and job outcomes separately; wages/employment cannot replace AI evidence.
Effects differ by activity: generated record drafts/reminders are not directly executable medication or nursing orders.

Human control points are revisiting orders/original monitoring data under institutional patient-identification/medication procedures, promptly reporting abnormalities and confirming state licensing/institutional authorization. AI cannot expand scope.
For an optional paper experiment, use only the fictional N01/N02 records and check any proposed draft against the originals. Do not upload real health records or carry out clinical actions.
Proposed test: ask for a draft organized from fictional source records, then check every statement manually. No time-saving, adoption or clinical result has been established here.
Check each item under institutional identification/medication procedures, confirm licensure/operating authorization and retain records. This page provides no complete clinical checklist.
This round's NBS industry table lists no Chinese wages exactly equivalent to U.S. LPN/LVN. Health/social work is context only; comparable Chinese occupational industry shares were not obtained.

Definition note: NBS 2025 annual average wages for urban non-private units are health/social work 146,266 yuan, resident services/repairs/other services 70,226 yuan and public administration/social security/social organizations 119,465 yuan. These are industry figures, not occupational medians or starting pay.

Mainland Chinese nursing practice requires registration and a nurse practice certificate. Article 7 of the Nurses Regulation sets education, clinical internship, qualification-examination and other registration conditions. Passing an examination, completing training and obtaining practice registration are distinct statuses. A roughly one-year U.S. LPN/LVN pathway does not automatically satisfy these requirements. Article 21 requires nursing supervision for clinical internships.
Insufficient evidence: No exact Chinese occupational wage distribution established; verified industry annual averages are context only, not individual starting pay/offers.
U.S. LPN/LVN pay and employment definitions

U.S. nationwide LPN/LVN May 2025 median annual pay is USD 64,400 (about USD 30.96/hour), with O*NET-displayed 2025 OEWS 10th through 90th percentiles USD 49,740—83,440. BLS projects 2025—2035 growth about 3% (about +19,700 people), average annual openings about 51,800 and 2025 employment about 666,900.

Fit signals: start with observable work behavior

Assess fit through tolerance for sustained shifts, standing/patient-moving demands and willingness to care under supervision/procedures. RIASEC and similar tools only generate hypotheses, not replace actual task experience.
Positive signals: Medication checks item by item under procedures, repeated-operation accuracy, patience/empathy with patients and recording/reporting abnormalities through procedures.

Caution conditions: Difficulty with shifts/physical demands, discomfort with blood/body fluids or serious illness, difficulty sustaining end-of-life/high-pressure work or impatience with detailed checking warrant caution.

Use the fictional N01/N02 exercise on this page to produce a discrepancy list and a list of unknowns or review questions. Ask another person whether each observation can be traced to the supplied source. This checks the paper record, not clinical skill.
O*NET lists SCR: Social, Conventional and Realistic. Helping people, working with procedures and practical activities are interests to explore, not evidence of licensure or clinical performance.

O*NET lists cooperation, attention to detail, dependability and stress tolerance, with service orientation, communication and coordination skills. These describe job tendencies, not hiring/licensing standards.
MBTI, Enneagram and similar type tools provide no occupational job evidence and serve only self-reflection; continue checking real tasks, boundaries and reviewable delivery.

Procedures beyond licensed authorization
Entry pathways and capability stages

U.S. LPN/LVNs must complete state-approved education (typically about 1 year), pass examinations and obtain licensure. Mainland China nursing practice qualifications are regulated by health authorities; verify separately.

United States: complete a state-approved practical/vocational nursing program, commonly a certificate or diploma offered by community colleges or technical schools, typically about one year and including supervised clinical experience. Check the destination nursing board’s eligibility, examination and licensing requirements; completion alone does not grant a license. Mainland Chinese nursing practice requires registration and a nurse practice certificate. Article 7 of the Nurses Regulation sets education, clinical internship, qualification-examination and other registration conditions. Passing an examination, completing training and obtaining practice registration are distinct statuses. A roughly one-year U.S. LPN/LVN pathway does not automatically satisfy these requirements. Article 21 requires nursing supervision for clinical internships.

Education, training evidence, licenses and job permissions are different statuses. Training completion is not licensure; competent authorities issue licenses defining scope. Mainland China and U.S. systems cannot substitute for one another.

After completing the required education and obtaining the applicable license, provide authorized basic care and maintain records under the required supervision. The specific setting determines which tasks are permitted; a novice paper exercise grants no clinical permission.

Before entry, use the fictional record discrepancy and unknowns lists only to explore careful checking. For actual practice, education, supervised training and authorized assessment are separate evidence; do not upload real patient records to this page.

First verify state-approved education, licensing exams and target-institution procedural authorization. Clinical practice occurs under compliant-program supervision; nursing-assistant experience does not automatically authorize medication/dressings or LPN/LVN licensure.

Some states allow experienced LPN/LVNs to supervise peers or unlicensed assistants, subject to both state/institutional requirements. RN transition requires relevant education, exams and registration; supervision experience does not automatically create a supervisory RN.
Market signals and transition directions
BLS projects 2025—2035 growth about 3% (about +19,700 people), average annual openings about 51,800. These are occupational statistics, not individual hiring probabilities or recruitment samples.

BLS and current O*NET both use 2025—2035: 666,900 in 2025 to about 686,700 in 2035; BLS separately lists net increase about 19,700 and annual openings 51,800. Endpoints/change are separately rounded; older periods are not retained as current comparisons.

Patient observation, source-based nursing records and team communication may be useful prior experience. They do not substitute for the RN role’s separate assessment, care-planning and qualification requirements.
Check the destination state’s RN education, examinations and licensing/registration requirements. LPN/LVN experience is not an automatic RN qualification.

items.answer: United States: complete a state-approved practical/vocational nursing program, commonly a certificate or diploma offered by community colleges or technical schools, typically about one year and including supervised clinical experience. Check the destination nursing board’s eligibility, examination and licensing requirements; completion alone does not grant a license. Mainland Chinese nursing practice requires registration and a nurse practice certificate. Article 7 of the Nurses Regulation sets education, clinical internship, qualification-examination and other registration conditions. Passing an examination, completing training and obtaining practice registration are distinct statuses. A roughly one-year U.S. LPN/LVN pathway does not automatically satisfy these requirements. Article 21 requires nursing supervision for clinical internships.

risks.consequence: Wrong medication or patient may cause harm.
risks.mitigation: Authorized personnel check under institutional medication/identification procedures, promptly referring doubts to responsible people; this is not a full clinical checklist.
risks.scenario: When patient identification or institutional medication checks are not implemented.

risks.mitigation: Respond and report promptly under applicable clinical and institutional procedures; completing documentation must not delay urgent care. Mainland Chinese nurses are separately subject to Article 17 of the Nurses Regulation.
risks.scenario: When abnormal vital signs are not promptly recorded/reported.

risks.consequence: Needlestick injuries/cross-infection affect patient and worker safety.
risks.mitigation: Follow the applicable infection-control training and Standard Precautions, including hand hygiene, appropriate protection and sharps handling. U.S. occupational exposures have separate OSHA reporting and follow-up requirements; this overview is not a procedure manual.
risks.scenario: When standard precautions are absent during injections, dressings or body-fluid handling.

risks.mitigation: Check applicable privacy rules, access permissions and institutional policy. Mainland nurses must protect patient privacy under Article 18; this page does not establish the full applicability of U.S. privacy law.
risks.scenario: When patient information, records or handovers disclose too broadly.

risks.mitigation: Stay within license scope; stop/refer to RNs/doctors beyond authorization.
risks.scenario: When assessment, medication or procedures exceed licensed authority.

risks.consequence: Incorrect records or missed abnormalities enter care workflows.
risks.mitigation: Review original orders/monitoring data and retain human-review records.
risks.scenario: When record drafts, reminders or trend alerts are accepted without checking.

subject.name: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
subject.summary: This page covers U.S. licensed practical and licensed vocational nurses (LPN/LVNs). They provide basic nursing care, generally under registered-nurse or physician supervision. Permitted duties and supervision depend on state rules and training. Mainland Chinese nursing registration and professional titles form a separate system; they are not equivalent LPN/LVN grades.
